title: OQF Stimulus
description: Schema for stimulus.json — a shared prompt (reading passage, diagram, code snippet, dataset, etc.) referenced by one or more question.json files via their `stimulus` field, so it's authored once and never duplicated across the questions that share it.

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor (e.g. VS Code) at this document's JSON Schema for inline validation/autocomplete. A JSON-tooling convention, not part of the OES content model — an OES parser ignores it like any other unrecognized field.

oqf_version.description: Any 0.2.x patch release of OQF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

id.description: Kebab-case. Must match this stimulus's folder name when co-located (referenced via a `path`).

title.description: Optional — many stimuli (a bare passage or diagram) don't need one; a consumer falls back to something generic like "Reading Passage" when absent.

content.description: The shared prompt, as Markdown. A string holds it inline; {file} points at a sibling Markdown file instead, conventionally "stimulus.md". Optional — a stimulus that is purely an image or dataset in assets/ has no prose at all. Prefer the inline form for anything published or referenced by URL: a content_hash over this document does not cover a separate file's bytes, so referenced prose can be swapped while the hash still verifies.

authors.description: GitHub usernames. A stimulus can be hosted and reused independently of any question, so it needs its own attribution.

source.description: Where this stimulus was originally sourced or adapted from, if it wasn't authored directly for OES — e.g. a reading passage produced by an importer against another platform's content. Entirely optional; omit for content authored directly. Distinct from this document's own top-level `license`, which describes this OES document's license, not what it was adapted from — the original may be more restrictive (or simply different) and belongs in `source.license` instead.

platform.description: Free-text label for the originating platform or site, e.g. "Khan Academy", "MIT OpenCourseWare". Deliberately not an enum — OES doesn't hard-code or endorse any specific platform; any importer fills in whatever's accurate.

license.description: The ORIGINAL content's license or terms of use at the source. Free text, not constrained to SPDX like this document's own `license` field — many platforms' terms of use aren't expressible as a single SPDX identifier.

retrieved_at.description: When this content was fetched/adapted from the source — provenance, and a signal for how stale this copy might be.

note.description: Free-text context an importer or author wants to record — adaptation details, attribution requirements, anything not covered by the fields above.
